terms.meaning: one number shown to a reader, together with its unit and where it came from.
a generated output a reader sees, such as a slide, chart or table.
a label such as millions of US dollars, percent, months or raw that says what a number measures.
a function that only uses its inputs and does no database or file work.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose, rule and imports
sections.what: Header comment that describes the job and the rule of extracting only what is shown, then imports the year check and the shared types.
sections.why: States the rule the whole file follows: count anything that appears on the page.
sections.watch_out: Anything displayed counts, so a new display format may need its own extraction.

sections.name: EVIDENCE_PATHS
sections.title: Evidence paths for each stored field
sections.what: A lookup table that maps each stored field name to the evidence path name that its evidence is filed under.
sections.why: Copied from the renderers so this file can run from a script without loading the display layer, as the comment says.
sections.watch_out: The table is a copy, so if the renderers change their names, this table drifts silently.

sections.name: UNITS
sections.title: Units for each field
sections.what: A lookup table that gives each field a unit: millions of US dollars for budgets, percent for cost deviation, months for delays, and raw for capacity.
sections.why: Lets readers and checks know what kind of number each field holds.
sections.watch_out: Fields such as plannedBudgetM sit beside plannedBudget, so a new field must be added to the table or it gets no unit.

sections.name: numeric
sections.title: Keeping only real numbers
sections.what: Returns a value only if it is a finite number. Text, empty values, and infinity become nothing, so they never reach the checker as numbers.
sections.why: Likely reason: it stops missing or text values from being checked as if they were measured numbers.
sections.watch_out: Numeric text such as '12' is dropped, even though it looks like a number.

sections.name: scrapeText
sections.title: Finding numbers inside slide text
sections.what: Pulls every number out of a line of slide text, such as a bullet, footnote, or title. Each one is labelled as having unknown origin.
sections.why: The code comment says the deck records no source for numbers written in prose, and marking them unknown is the honest finding.
sections.watch_out: Every number in the text becomes a claim, including years and footnote numbers, so the report can count them.

sections.name: extractLessonsLearntNumerals (part 1)
sections.title: Lessons learnt deck: first part of numbers
sections.what: Reads the summary data of the lessons learnt deck and returns the numbers it shows. Project budgets and delays are marked as reported, so they must be traced to evidence. Totals and overrun percentages are marked as derived, so they must match a stored calculation.
sections.why: Reported values need a lookup key so the gate can find their evidence. Derived values need a calculation record.
sections.watch_out: The kind assigned here decides which check applies. A wrong kind can make a correct number look untraceable.

sections.name: extractLessonsLearntNumerals: for
sections.title: Lessons learnt deck: pillars, sub-drivers, slides
sections.what: Continues the same reading for pillar counts, sub-driver counts, chart values, and the text of slide bullets, footnotes, and titles. Charts and counts are treated as derived. Text is scanned for numbers.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It follows the same pattern of treating counts as derived and prose numbers as unknown.
sections.watch_out: Every number in slide bullets is scanned, so a single sentence can create several claims.

sections.name: extractRealityScanNumerals
sections.title: Reality Scan results
sections.what: Reads the totals and each project's fields from a Reality Scan result. Fields the artifact marks as calculated are derived. Other fields are reported and receive a lookup so evidence can be found.
sections.why: The code comment says 'calculated' is the artifact's own word for derived, so the extractor follows it.
sections.watch_out: Any field marked as stored or directly reported is treated as a claim that must trace back to evidence.

sections.name: extractDatumNumerals (part 1)
sections.title: Datum slides: cost and schedule values
sections.what: Reads each project's planned budget, actual budget, cost deviation, schedule slip, and capacity from the datum slide set. Each one is added as a reported claim with its verbatim wording when present.
sections.why: Reported values must trace to evidence, so each one gets a lookup key.
sections.watch_out: The function expects each field to have a value and optional verbatim text in a fixed shape. A different shape means the field is silently skipped.

sections.name: extractDatumNumerals: if
sections.title: Datum slides: recalculated overruns and averages
sections.what: Recomputes cost overrun percentages, slip in years, and the slide averages, the same way the slide does in the browser. These are marked as derived, and the plotted count is recorded.
sections.why: The code comment says the slide computes these in the browser with no calculation record, so the gate must flag them.
sections.watch_out: These values will be untraceable unless a matching calculation record exists. The rounding here must stay the same as the slide's rounding, or matches fail.

summary: Turns each rendered artifact into the list of numbers it shows to a reader, along with the source each number claims.
purpose: Lists every number a reader would see in a generated slide, chart or table, so those numbers can be checked against the stored data.
why: The header says to extract what is actually rendered, not what is convenient, and that a count printed inside a slide bullet counts too. Only the first 41 lines were in the packet, so the reason for the rest is not visible.
how: Only the opening was in the packet. From it: the file takes loaded artifact payloads, maps stored field names to evidence paths and to units, and pulls numbers from them. The function bodies, lines 42 to 287, were not visible.
inputs: Already-loaded artifact payloads and the stored project fields they show. The harness does the loading.
outputs: A list of numeral claims, each with the number and a unit hint. The unit hint comes from the lookup table.
risks: A field missing from the unit table gets no unit hint. Evidence path names are copied locally, so they can drift from the renderers that they mirror.
debug: When a number is missing or has the wrong unit, check the evidence path and unit tables for that field name. Check that bullet text is scanned, since the header says it should be. The remaining functions were not in the packet.
